Title: Verify that worker holiday retrieval for a worker is restricted to authorized users only, even with pagination
Preconditions: User A is authenticated and owns Worker X. User B is authenticated and does not own Worker X. Worker X has at least one holiday recorded.
Steps:
1. Authenticate as User B. 2. Send a GET request to /api/worker-holidays/{workerId}?page=0&limit=10 with workerId set to Worker X's ID. 3. Observe the response.

Test Data: workerId = [ID of Worker X owned by User A]
Expected Result: The API responds with HTTP status 403 Forbidden and an error message 'Access Denied'. No holidays for Worker X are returned.

Title: Verify that negative page or limit values are rejected for worker holiday search
Section: Worker Holiday Management - Pagination Input Validation
Preconditions: User is authenticated and owns Worker X. Worker X has at least one holiday recorded.
Steps:

Test Data: workerId = [ID of Worker X]
Expected Result: 1. The API responds with HTTP status 400 Bad Request and an error message indicating invalid page value. 2. The API responds with HTTP status 400 Bad Request and an error message indicating invalid limit value.

Title: Verify that a user cannot update a worker holiday for a worker they do not manage
Section: Worker Holiday Management - Insecure Direct Object Reference
Preconditions: User A is authenticated and owns Worker X. User B is authenticated and does not own Worker X. Worker X has a holiday with ID H1.
Steps:
1. Authenticate as User B. 2. Send a PUT request to /api/worker-holidays/{holidayId} with the payload in testData, setting holidayId to H1. 3. Observe the response.

Test Data: {"holidayDate": "2024-12-26", "reason": "Updated Reason"}
Expected Result: The API responds with HTTP status 403 Forbidden and an error message 'Access Denied'. The holiday is not updated.

Title: Verify that worker holiday reason is not exposed in conflict error responses
Section: Worker Holiday Management - Sensitive Data Exposure
Preconditions: User is authenticated and owns Worker X. Worker X already has a holiday on 2024-12-25 with reason 'Sensitive Personal Reason'.
Steps:
1. Authenticate as the user. 2. Send a PUT request to /api/worker-holidays/{holidayId} with the payload in testData, setting holidayId to the ID of the existing holiday. 3. Observe the response.

Test Data: {"holidayDate": "2024-12-25", "reason": "New Reason"}
Expected Result: The API responds with HTTP status 200 OK and the message 'Worker already has a holiday on 2024-12-25'. The reason 'Sensitive Personal Reason' is NOT included in the response body.

Title: Verify that rapid successive requests to add worker holidays are rate-limited to prevent abuse
Preconditions: User is authenticated and owns Worker X. Worker X has no holidays recorded.
Steps:
1. Authenticate as the user. 2. Rapidly send 20 POST requests to /api/worker-holidays/add?workerId={workerId} with the payload in testData, varying the holidayDate for each request. 3. Observe the response for the 20th request.

Test Data: [{"holidayDate": "2024-12-01", "reason": "Holiday 1"}, {"holidayDate": "2024-12-02", "reason": "Holiday 2"}, ...]
Expected Result: The API responds with HTTP status 429 Too Many Requests for the 20th request, or the 20th request is rejected with an appropriate error message. No more than 10 holidays are added to the system within the rate limit window.
